message.content:
Fix one open Entire finding on PR 474 (branch `feat/one-shot-heap-budget`, trail 404, change 272). Start from `origin/feat/one-shot-heap-budget` (`git fetch origin` first); commit locally; I push. Read /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md and crates/semantic/src/heap.rs (the cgroup reader around lines 102-150).
Finding (crates/semantic/src/heap.rs:127-129): on cgroup v1 systems where the memory controller shares a mount with other controllers (e.g. `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,memory`), the hard-coded `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/...` path misses every limit file. `cgroup_limit()` silently ignores the failed reads, so `HeapBudget::machine()` uses host memory and can allow 8 GiB inside a 2 GiB container. Fix: resolve the hierarchy's mount point and root from `/proc/self/mountinfo` (find the `cgroup` fs-type entry whose super options include `memory` for v1, and the `cgroup2` entry for v2) and build the limit paths from that mount point plus the process's cgroup path from `/proc/self/cgroup` (keep the existing ancestor walk and `min` over ancestors). Keep the parsing pure (functions taking the file contents as &str) so it is unit-tested with fixture strings: a v1 comounted `cpu,cpuacct,memory` mountinfo line, a v1 separate `memory` mount, a v2 line, a mountinfo with no cgroup line, a bind-mounted root (field 4 not `/`), and malformed lines (must not panic). Then the unreadable/absent case must not be silent in a harmful way: when no limit can be found, fall back to the host figure as today, but say in the doc comment exactly that. First failing tests are the fixtures above. Do not add dependencies. Gates: `just lint doc-check machete typos` and nextest `-p caliper-docgen-semantic` (the heap module); report exit codes. No oracle runs, no corpora. Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/, rust 1.99.1 first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin). Cap 40 tool calls. Final message at most 50 words: SHA, tests, gates.
